chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: Rene Hall, Earl Palmer and Rod Pierce set up Rendezvous sessions
summary: Hall, Palmer and others plan sessions under Fields' name and sell the idea to producer Rod Pierce of Rendezvous.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: So I had to leave California (inaudible), and that's when Rene and Earl and all of them got together and organized this music master, a recording master or something, that they were going to do it and pay and then peddle the thing. Then they said they were going to make Ernie Fields the leader.
In other words, they produced their own record?
Yeah, and they were going to make Ernie Fields the leader.
So they said that to me, will I do this. I had left town and they said what they
had in mind, what we've gone through and they said in this way nobody has to be there but you, we're going to do it and get everything and be responsible--
You don't have to use your own band.
Incidentally, Irving Ashby is the man we're thinking about. Irving Ashby is the guitar player, he had a tendency to drink.

I said I'll buy it. I said I'll be happy and they said okay. They said when I figure I can come out there we will do this and everything, and what we can do, we can overdub some of this and players can do so and so and so on. So I said okay, I'll buy that, just look forward whenever you can and while we were waiting to get that chance, he gets in with Rod Pierce, Rendevous, producer with Rendevous and he kind of liked the idea.

So Rod Pierce told them, you don't need to be making no record if you're not going to go anywhere, you got to get out. So they all told him we've got that covered, it's going to be Ernie Fields' band, and so Rod Pierce said I'll buy that then.
